label: Reader & Writer Identity
raw_text: Build an identity as a reader and writer, developing a repertoire of resources and tools to continuously expand participation as an active consumer and producer of texts.
child_texts: Generate, understand, monitor, and discuss personal and academic reading and writing goals, revising as appropriate. (I/C)
Discuss or write about personal and academic reading and writing preferences, referring to specific techniques, topics, modes, and genres that resonate most. (I/C)
Select, read, and write texts of personal interest and academic relevance to grade-level texts and topics. (I/C)
Build a repertoire of comprehension and composition skills, strategies, and techniques, drawing from them as needed to aid the interpretation and construction of texts. (I/C)

Participate in a community of readers and writers by developing group norms, discussing texts, sharing individual writing, listening as others share their writing, and offering and responding to feedback. (I/C)
Develop independence and autonomy as a reader and writer. (I/C)
competency_statement: Build a personal identity as a reader and writer by developing and using a variety of skills, strategies, and tools to actively engage with and create texts.
observable_behaviors: Set and revise personal and academic reading and writing goals.
Discuss or write about reading and writing preferences with examples of techniques, topics, modes, and genres.
Choose and engage with texts that interest them and relate to academic topics.
Use a range of comprehension and composition strategies to understand and create texts.
Participate in group discussions about texts and writing, share their own writing, listen to others, and give and receive feedback.
Demonstrate growing independence in reading and writing tasks.
skill_clauses: Generate, understand, monitor, and revise personal and academic reading and writing goals.
Discuss or write about personal and academic reading and writing preferences with reference to specific techniques, topics, modes, and genres.
Select, read, and write texts of personal interest and academic relevance.
Build and draw from a repertoire of comprehension and composition skills, strategies, and techniques to interpret and construct texts.
Participate in a community of readers and writers by developing group norms, discussing texts, sharing writing, listening to others, and offering and responding to feedback.
Develop independence and autonomy as a reader and writer.
